label: Land
description: A greenfield Azure deployment for a single workload with no existing cloud estate to integrate. The focus is getting the foundation right — landing zone design, identity, networking baseline, and first workload deployment.
scope: Single workload, single subscription, no hybrid connectivity required
keyPatterns: Hub-spoke virtual network (simplified — single hub, one spoke)
Microsoft Entra ID baseline (MFA, Conditional Access)
Single-region deployment with Availability Zone spread
Azure Monitor + Application Insights baseline
Azure Backup for data protection
Basic Azure Policy assignments (Security Benchmark)
iacReadiness: IaC can begin after Step 2. Governance boundary is thin at this tier — management groups and policy are lightweight.

steps.notes: Discovery sessions require customer follow-up time — RTO/RPO, compliance status, and data residency are rarely confirmed in a single meeting
Conditional Access sign-off, VNet/NSG design, Policy baseline, and Log Analytics setup each require stakeholder alignment cycles
Data classification workshop plus customer validation time; documented replication strategy and lifecycle policy take longer than the discovery
Compute selection, VNet topology, autoscale configuration — design documentation and review cycles add time even at this tier
Proper failure matrix requires enumerating components, running failure scenarios, identifying SPOFs, and documenting remediation — not a half-day exercise
Pre-deployment guardrails include approved tiers, lifecycle policies, tagging policy, and budgets; RI and Savings Plan decisions wait for 30-60 days of utilization data
IaC repo structure, CI/CD pipeline with proper gates, deployment safety pattern selection, and minimum runbook library — more than two days of work

label: Scale
description: An existing Azure estate with multiple workloads and integration requirements — on-premises connectivity, third-party SaaS, or multiple product teams sharing platform infrastructure. Platform engineering patterns become necessary.
scope: Multi-workload, multiple subscriptions, hybrid connectivity, shared services
keyPatterns: Azure Virtual WAN or mature hub-spoke with multiple spokes
Subscription vending (automated provisioning for new teams)
Azure Policy baseline initiative (Security Benchmark + custom)
Privileged Identity Management (PIM) — no standing Owner
Log Analytics workspace hierarchy with Sentinel
Azure Cost Management tagging strategy + budgets
ExpressRoute or VPN Gateway for hybrid connectivity
Private Endpoints for all production PaaS
iacReadiness: Step 2 is the critical path. Management group topology, Policy initiative scope, and network design must be finalized before IaC templates are authored — changing these post-deployment requires resource moves.

steps.notes: Multiple workload SLAs to reconcile across teams; plan for 3–4 discovery sessions, not one — stakeholder availability is a consistent constraint
Management groups, subscription topology, Policy initiatives, Private Endpoints at scale, Sentinel onboarding — expect multiple review cycles and sign-off delays from IAM, network, and security teams
Multiple data stores with different replication requirements; data gravity analysis requires cross-team input and documentation review
Virtual WAN or hub-spoke decision, multi-team network alignment, ExpressRoute lead time planning (4–8 weeks carrier provisioning starts here)
Larger failure domain surface; on-premises dependency chain adds complexity — thorough failure matrix and remediation planning is a full week of work
Multi-team tagging, budgets, lifecycle policies, and cost ownership are set before go-live; commitment purchases require post-launch utilization evidence and Finance alignment
Multi-team GitOps, environment promotion gates, change management process — integration friction across teams is unavoidable

label: Govern
description: Regulated workloads operating at enterprise scale — multi-region, multi-product-team, with a dedicated platform team managing landing zones. Compliance policy stacks, FinOps maturity, and formal change management are non-negotiable.
scope: Multi-region, multi-subscription, dedicated platform team, compliance mandates
keyPatterns: Azure Landing Zone (ALZ) reference implementation
Enterprise-scale management group hierarchy
Azure Policy compliance stacks (FedRAMP, HIPAA, PCI, NIST 800-53)
Multi-region active-active or active-passive topology
Azure Virtual WAN with ExpressRoute primary + VPN failover
Defender for Cloud Plan 2 on all subscriptions
FinOps maturity model — Walk to Run level
Formal CAB (Change Advisory Board) process
Sovereign cloud considerations (Azure Government for FedRAMP High)
iacReadiness: Step 2 is the long pole at this tier — management group hierarchy, Policy initiative stacks, and network topology definition can take 4–8 weeks. No Bicep template should be authored until the governance boundary is signed off. Rushing this creates technical debt that is expensive to remediate.

steps.notes: Multiple regulatory frameworks require legal and compliance input; data residency constraints across BUs, competing SLA requirements — plan for 4–6 sessions across different stakeholder groups

Full ALZ deployment, custom Policy initiatives, Sentinel enterprise onboarding, multi-region network design — this is a multi-month workstream. Sign-off involves IAM, network, security, compliance, and legal teams.
Data sovereignty across regions, zero-RPO requirements, cross-region replication compliance — legal and compliance review extends every data architecture decision
Multi-region active-active or active-passive decision, ExpressRoute + VPN coexistence design, per-region compute strategy — ExpressRoute carrier provisioning (4–8 weeks) starts in parallel
Full failure matrix for regulated incident scenarios, POA&M for identified gaps, compliance evidence packaging — documentation alone takes days
FinOps maturity assessment, chargeback implementation, cost policy guardrails, and a 3-year commitment review plan — Finance and procurement alignment adds calendar time
CAB integration, ATO documentation package, ConMon program standup, enterprise runbook library — regulatory documentation alone is weeks of work
